product_one_liner.value: Axure RP helps UX designers, product managers, analysts, and developers create interactive prototypes without coding and share them through Axure Cloud for feedback and developer handoff.
product_one_liner.notes: Axure describes its intended users, no-code interactive UX prototyping, and sharing through Axure Cloud for feedback and development handoff. Source: https://linkedin.com/company/axure-software-solutions

pricing_page.notes: Axure has a public pricing page listing its plans, including an Enterprise plan with contact-based pricing. Source: https://www.axure.com/pricing

named_customers.notes: named_customers: Axure's customer page explicitly describes PROS and Syncron using Axure RP prototypes. These are customers, not merely partners or investors. Source: https://www.axure.com/axure-customers | named_customers.0: Axure's customer page describes PROS creating customer demos and collecting feedback using Axure RP. Source: https://www.axure.com/axure-customers | named_customers.1: Axure's customer page explicitly states that Syncron teams use Axure RP prototypes. Source: https://www.axure.com/axure-customers

employee_band.notes: The company profile reports 17 employees, which falls within 11-20. Profile-associated employee counts may differ from actual payroll headcount. Source: https://linkedin.com/company/axure-software-solutions

hq_location.notes: hq_city: Axure's company profile lists San Diego, California as its location. Source: https://linkedin.com/company/axure-software-solutions | hq_country: Axure's company profile lists its location as San Diego, California, United States. Source: https://linkedin.com/company/axure-software-solutions

founded_year.notes: Axure's company profile explicitly lists 2002 as its founding year. Source: https://linkedin.com/company/axure-software-solutions

eng_blog.notes: The readable blog index contains product announcements, lifecycle updates, tutorials, compliance news, and UX articles; it does not show the required two engineer-authored articles explaining how Axure is built. Source: https://www.axure.com/blog

public_docs.notes: Axure maintains public documentation and a reference guide with getting-started materials, tutorials, and an interactive-button tutorial, meeting the multiple-article requirement. Sources: https://docs.axure.com/ and https://www.axure.com/support

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The careers page lists only Senior Software Engineer, with no qualifying AI, ML, or data-science role title. Source: https://www.axure.com/careers

model_provider.notes: No in-product AI model or provider was identified after reviewing product documentation, security information, the blog, privacy policy, and the subprocessor list. The MCP documentation describes customers connecting their own AI tools; compatibility with Claude or ChatGPT does not establish that Axure itself uses either provider. Sources: https://docs.axure.com/axure-rp/reference/mcp, https://docs.axure.com/axure-cloud/reference/MCP, https://www.axure.com/security, https://www.axure.com/blog, https://www.axure.com/privacy, and https://www.axure.com/gdpr

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: Axure names SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications and publicly states its commitment to GDPR compliance. Its PCI claim is narrower: Axure says it is PCI compliant for transmitting card information, while PCI DSS Level 1 specifically describes its third-party processor, not an Axure-wide Level 1 certification. Sources: https://www.axure.com/security and https://www.axure.com/gdpr | compliance_certs.0: Axure explicitly names its SOC 2 Type II certification on https://www.axure.com/security. | compliance_certs.1: Axure explicitly claims ISO 27001 certification on https://www.axure.com/security. | compliance_certs.2: Axure publicly states its commitment to GDPR compliance. This is a compliance statement rather than a separate certification claim. Source: https://www.axure.com/gdpr | compliance_certs.3: The security page claims PCI compliance for Axure's transmission of card information and names PCI DSS Level 1 for its payment processor. This entry is limited to payment processing and does not assert that Axure itself holds Level 1 certification. Source: https://www.axure.com/security

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: Dealroom reports no known external funding, and Latka describes Axure as self-funded with no outside investment, supporting stage none. Sources: https://app.dealroom.co/companies/axure_software_solutions and http://getlatka.com/companies/axure | funding_date: The sources identify no outside funding round, so a funding-round date is not applicable and is left null. Consequently there is no applicable round amount; null does not imply a zero-dollar round. Sources: https://app.dealroom.co/companies/axure_software_solutions and http://getlatka.com/companies/axure

raised_18mo.notes: The funding sources describe Axure as having no known outside funding, supporting false for a funding raise during the eighteen-month window. Sources: https://app.dealroom.co/companies/axure_software_solutions and http://getlatka.com/companies/axure

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The careers page lists only Senior Software Engineer and no SDR, BDR, sales/business-development representative, or account-executive opening. Source: https://www.axure.com/careers

launched_6mo.notes: On September 24, 2026, Axure announced an experimental built-in MCP server giving AI tools access to RP designs for code generation, analysis, and documentation. This is a substantive new capability within the six-month window, not merely a UI adjustment or bug fix. Source: https://www.axure.com/changelog/2026-09-24

leadership_change_12mo.notes: Unknown: no dated C-level or VP appointment or departure was found for the twelve-month window. The company page at https://www.axure.com/company does not provide a complete leadership roster with start dates, so it cannot substantiate a negative answer.
